background: ING Groep is the holding company of the Netherlands' largest bank, a digital-first retail and wholesale bank funded by deposits across the Netherlands, Belgium, Germany and other European markets, lending on mortgages and to corporates worldwide.
synthesis: Fitch rates the group A+ and S&P A-, both stable, with the last move Fitch's upgrade to A+ on 14 Apr 2016. Capital is on the weak side of EU and Nordic peers: CET1 of 13.0% and leverage of 4.3% are both in the bottom quarter against medians of 16.4% and 5.5%, and both have fallen since 30 Jun 2024, CET1 by 1.0 points and leverage by 0.3 points. Liquidity is mixed, with LCR of 139% in the bottom quarter and NSFR of 128% above the 124% median. The flagged news is a strong quarter on 30 Jul 2026 and, on 2 Sep 2026, an Australian capital add-on after the local unit overstated its liquidity, a control finding rather than a solvency one.
